decisions.reason: The underground mining loaders remain a core option whose long sales cycles keep demand uncertainty unresolved, and the low marginal cost of retaining the option justifies keeping it open.
The dump trucks are a related option in the same underground market, so the firm keeps this option alive while uncertainty persists and the cost of doing so is low.
The construction dumper fits the firm's construction segment and, despite being a more standard product, its modest keeping cost and still-unresolved demand make the option worth holding.

The inclined furniture lift is a niche option with weak strategic fit whose value has likely not materialized after three years, so the firm abandons it to release resources to more promising options.
The inclined building material lift is closer to the firm's construction and material handling core, so the firm keeps the option open at low cost while assessing contractor adoption.
The truck-mounted inclined furniture lift is an even more specialized niche option that has likely shown limited market value, prompting the firm to drop it and redeploy resources.
